title: Braised Pork Belly
subtitle: Slow-braised pork belly with cider and root vegetables
excerpt: Pork belly braised slowly with cider, onion, and root vegetables until the meat is completely tender and the skin blistered and crisp under a final blast of heat. One of the best things you can do with a cut that rewards patience.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pork belly as a braising cut has become much more widely used in British cooking since the 1990s, when cheaper cuts began to be rehabilitated in professional kitchens and spread to home cooking. The combination of pork with apple and cider is a long-standing British tradition, particularly in the west of England, rooted in the productive pairing of pigs kept in orchards.

recipeTools.notes: A deep roasting tin with foil or a lid.

content.text: Score the skin of the pork belly deeply with a sharp knife before cooking, down to but not through the fat. The salt rubbed into the scores will draw out moisture and help the skin blister and crackle. The long braise in cider will keep the meat moist. The final step is uncovering and raising the temperature to blister and crisp the skin, so do not skip it.
Score the skin and rub salt vigorously into the cuts. Leave uncovered in the fridge overnight, or at room temperature for at least 1 hour before cooking.

Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Spread the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay, thyme, and apple in the base of a deep roasting tin. Pour in the cider and stock. Place the pork belly skin-side up on top of the vegetables. Cover tightly with foil.
Braise in the oven for 2.5 hours until the meat is completely tender when tested with a skewer, it should meet no resistance.

Remove the foil. Increase the oven to 230 C / fan 210 C / gas 8. Return the pork for 20 to 30 minutes until the skin is well blistered and crackling. If it colours unevenly, move the tin closer to the top of the oven. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing. Strain the braising liquid and serve as a sauce.
